Credit union money:
insured or not?

lines.text: Think your credit union money isn't insured? That's a myth.
lines.say: Think your credit union money isn't insured? That's a myth.

lines.text: At federally insured credit unions, deposits are covered up to $250,000 per member, per ownership category.
lines.say: At federally insured credit unions, deposits are covered up to two hundred fifty thousand dollars per member, per ownership category.

lines.text: It's NCUA insurance, backed by the full faith and credit of the United States, like FDIC.
lines.say: It's N C U A insurance, backed by the full faith and credit of the United States, like F D I C.

lines.text: NCUA says members have never lost a penny of insured savings.
lines.say: N C U A says members have never lost a penny of insured savings.

scene.text: Credit union members have never lost a penny of insured savings at a federally insured credit union.

lines.text: Example: your own account, $250,000; a joint account with two owners, $500,000.
lines.say: Example: your own account, two hundred fifty thousand; a joint account with two owners, five hundred thousand.

post.title: Credit union money isn't insured? Myth, up to $250,000
post.ig:
Think your credit union money isn't insured? That's a myth.
Federally insured credit unions: deposits covered up to $250,000 per member, per ownership category, by NCUA's Share Insurance Fund, backed by the full faith and credit of the US government.
NCUA: "Credit union members have never lost a penny of insured savings at a federally insured credit union."
As of June 30, 2026: 4,214 federally insured credit unions, 146.1 million members (down from 6,021 credit unions at the end of 2015).
Not covered: stocks, bonds, annuities, crypto. A few state-chartered credit unions use private insurer ASI (106 in 10 states as of 2021).
Sources: NCUA, NCUA Quarterly Data Summary Q2 2026, ASI letter to the Federal Reserve (2021).
News and education, not financial advice.
